title: AUTH-007 MFA Factor, Challenge and Recovery Lifecycle

derivedStateRules.when: two_factor_enabled=0 and no verified factor is authoritative
a factor exists with verified=0; this state grants no MFA assurance
two_factor_enabled=1 AND verified=1 AND mfa_enrolled_at is a valid timestamp AND lockedUntil is absent or expired
the authoritative factor has a future lockedUntil; verification must fail closed until lock expiry

stateDomains.name: signInChallenge
stateDomains.stateSource: Better Auth signed two_factor challenge cookie and its server-side verification record

derivedStateRules.when: a signed, identity-bound, purpose-bound challenge exists and has not expired or been consumed
one valid TOTP or recovery-code verification completes the challenge exactly once
the challenge expiry timestamp is not later than the authoritative current time
identity, account state, factor, code, replay guard, or challenge validation fails

securityInvariants: Only W02 derives factor state from authoritative D1-01 records.
A pending or unverified factor never satisfies the L5-L8 MFA gate.
A privileged session must be created after verified MFA activation; pre-existing sessions are revoked on enable and disable.
Every accepted TOTP time-step is atomically consumed once per factor.
A sign-in challenge is identity-bound, purpose-bound, short-lived and single-use.
Recovery codes are encrypted at rest, consumed once, and replaced atomically on rotation.
Disable and recovery-code rotation require current-password reauthentication and valid TOTP step-up.
No client-supplied subject, role, layer, assurance flag, factor status, or challenge status is trusted.
MFA responses are no-store; factor secrets, plaintext recovery codes after issuance, replay state and lockout internals never appear in public DTOs.

effects: create exactly one pending TOTP factor
return provisioning URI and recovery codes once
keep privileged MFA assurance false

guards: authoritative read-back shows enabled=1, verified=1 and a valid enrollment timestamp
effects: mark the same factor verified
stamp enrollment time
revoke all pre-existing sessions
require a fresh login before privileged authority is restored
remove or disable the current factor
clear the enrollment timestamp and pending idempotency markers
revoke all existing sessions
deny privileged authority until MFA is re-enrolled and verified
atomically replace the full recovery-code set
invalidate every prior recovery code
return the new plaintext set exactly once
never return stored recovery-code material in status or audit responses

guards: challenge unexpired and bound to this identity
valid fresh TOTP time-step or unused recovery code
trust-device bypass not requested or accepted
effects: consume the challenge and factor proof once
issue the authenticated browser cookie or native session header only
never include the session credential in JSON
deny authentication
do not issue a session credential

guards: invalid code, inactive account, replay, malformed challenge or exhausted attempt budget
effects: deny authentication
increment or honor authoritative attempt/lockout controls
return a bounded public error without factor or account-enumeration details

x-forbidden.reason: MFA cannot become effective without successful verification of the pending factor.
client-supplied enabled, verified, layer or assurance flags cannot authorize the transition.
disable without both current-password and valid-TOTP step-up is forbidden.
a rejected challenge cannot later be reused.

reconciliation.statusRule: This state machine is contracted but not verified until production D1 migration/read-back, live W01/W02 integration, positive/negative/replay/concurrency security E2E, audit-event admission and final Mapping 0 evidence are accepted.
reconciliation.note: This contract describes the intended factor/challenge transitions; it does not assert that production schema or runtime acceptance has already occurred.
